coverage: Pier & Point covers four sites on San Francisco's central waterfront: Mission Rock, Mission Bay, Pier 70 and Potrero Power Station. A parcel that is not in this data is outside coverage, not "no activity".

record.name: P7
names: Mission Bay Future Parks -- P7 (active recreation)
record.summary: San Francisco Recreation and Parks describes parcels P7 and P9, under I-280 along Mission Bay Drive and Owens Street, as currently undeveloped and anticipated to house active uses such as a skate park, pickleball courts and a ballfield, fully funded through OCII, with construction beginning late 2028 and opening early 2030.

notes.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- computed from real DataSF street/curb data plus a stopping line drawn by Pier & Point (not a surveyed parcel or GIS file from the project team). The north edge follows the street edge exactly as estimated from DataSF's official street centerlines; the east edge is held off Owens St and the roundabout island by extra clearance rather than the standard street width alone. The south edge is a line drawn by Pier & Point, not a mapped street or parcel boundary -- there is real bare ground between it and the two buildings further south that isn't included here. The P9/P7 split is a straight line, not sourced to any drawn plan boundary. SF Rec & Park's Mission Bay Future Parks Project page names P7 & P9 as future 'Active Recreation' parks (anticipated skate park, pickleball courts and a ballfield), fully funded through OCII, with construction to begin late 2028 and opening early 2030; no schematic design specific to P7 was found.
notes.digitized_from: Computed from DataSF's official street centerlines, with extra generous clearance around Owens St's own centerline and around the P10 roundabout island, rather than hand-traced from imagery. The north edge follows Mission Bay Dr's street edge all the way up to the roundabout; the east edge is held clear of Owens St and of the P10 island by that extra clearance; the south edge is a line drawn by Pier & Point on a marked-up image and transferred to the map by automatic image matching (the same way as for P11/P11A), confirming the parcel stops well short of the two real buildings further south.

changes.text: Added a sourced dossier for Mission Bay Future Parks: P7 (active recreation).

The notes said no named, funded project had been found for P7. SF Rec & Park's Mission Bay Future Parks Project page names P7 and P9 as future active-recreation parks (skate park, pickleball courts, ballfield) fully funded through OCII, with construction to begin in late 2028, so that caveat was replaced and the page is now cited for the planned status and park use. The 'construction staging materials' description is now labelled an imagery observation, and an out-of-date note saying the neighbouring P8 record had been removed was corrected.

open_questions: No design, program or budget amount for P7 specifically was found: every source read treats P7 and P9 together, and the park program (skate park, pickleball, ballfield) is described as 'anticipated'. No P7-specific schematic design was found.

Dates conflict slightly between sources: Rec and Park's background text says the remaining parks 'are anticipated to be complete by 2028', while its schedule gives construction beginning late 2028 and opening early 2030, and OCII's November 2024 deck shows transfer to Rec and Park at the end of 2028 upon completion. The milestones above use the schedule table.
Which design team was selected (the August 2025 update said by mid-October 2025) was not found. Contractor not found.
'Bare and graded with construction equipment visible' in the geometry notes is an imagery observation; no source read says so.
The P9/P7 boundary in the geometry is a straight line drawn by this project; no source read draws or states it.

record.notes: OCII plan parcel P7 (labelled on the OCII Dec 2015 Attachment B map southwest of the P10 roundabout, east of P9). Sits within the same open-space band as P2, P9 and P8 (see each one's own record), immediately southwest of the Mission Bay Circle roundabout. SF Rec & Park says P7 & P9 are currently undeveloped; in USDA NAIP imagery (viewed 2026-09-29) the ground is bare and graded with construction equipment and materials visible.
